program_name: Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English) — and unusually well documented at course level for this programme, which makes the trilingualism verifiable rather than nominal. The brochure states 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. The published course-offering list for the programme shows teaching languages distributed roughly evenly across the three languages, with core compulsory subjects genuinely delivered in German and Italian, not only in English: Micro and Macroeconomics (8 CP, 1st year, compulsory) is taught in GERMAN; Tourism and Sport Law (6 CP, 1st year, compulsory) and Managerial Economics for TSE (6 CP, 2nd year, compulsory) are taught in ITALIAN; Marketing (8 CP, 1st year), Introduction to Management (6 CP), Introduction to Tourism, Sport and Event Management (6 CP), Introduction to Finance (8 CP), Introduction to Accounting for TSE (8 CP) and Managerial Accounting (6 CP) are taught in ENGLISH. A snapshot of the course-offering page yielded approximately 7 English, 6 Italian and 4 German courses plus Spanish/French language courses. In addition, year 1 requires TWO of the three 'Foreign Language – Communication and Presentation Skills in Specialized Language' courses (3 CP each) and students may NOT sit those exams in the language of their secondary-school final exam; year 2 adds a further compulsory 6 CP Foreign Language course in Spanish or French. unibz does not publish an official percentage split of teaching hours per language. [uncertain]
campus: Bruneck-Brunico — but this is a MOVING campus and the detail is decision-critical. The 2026/27 brochure states: 'Campus: Bruneck-Brunico, NOI Techpark Bruneck-Brunico' and classes take place both at the Bruneck-Brunico campus and at the NOI Techpark Bruneck-Brunico. However, the same brochure states: 'Students beginning their studies in the 2026/27 academic year at the Bruneck-Brunico Campus will continue their studies at the Bozen-Bolzano Campus starting from the second year, 2027/28.' So a student entering in 2026/27 spends ONLY year 1 in Bruneck-Brunico (Puster Valley, roughly 80 km northeast of Bolzano) and then relocates to the Bozen-Bolzano main campus for years 2 and 3. This is part of a wider wind-down of the Bruneck site: the Master in Tourism Management at Bruneck is suspended for 2026/27. Practical implication: accommodation, cost of living and travel planning differ between year 1 and years 2-3.
degree_class: L-18 (Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale / Economics and Business Administration). CONFIRMED — the task brief flagged this as 'to be verified' and it is now verified from two independent official sources: the 2026/27 brochure 'At a glance' box states 'Bachelor class: L-18', and both 2026/27 ranking-list PDFs are headed 'Ammissione al corso di laurea in L-18 Management del Turismo, dello Sport e degli Eventi' / 'Zulassung zum Bachelor in L-18 Tourismus-, Sport- und Eventmanagement'. The admission PDF also uses L-18 as its own example when explaining the double-enrolment rule ('the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., L-18/L-18').
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with competitive ranking — but in practice non-selective for EU applicants in 2026/27 (see selection_scoring). No entrance examination, no TOLC, no SAT, no CENT-S, no interview and no portfolio. Selection is a document- and grade-based dossier evaluation performed by the Admission Committee on the basis of self-declared secondary-school grades plus language-certificate bonus points. Applications are submitted through the unibz Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/). Separate quotas and procedures apply to (1) EU citizens and those given parity of treatment and (2) non-EU citizens living abroad. Selection criteria approved by Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025 — the same resolution that governs the other Faculty of Economics bachelor programmes.
academic_requirements: A secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system, OR an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if it was obtained after 12 years of education AND at least the last two years were attended within that foreign school system (unibz gives the Irish Leaving Certificate as the counter-example: attending only one year and obtaining the certificate is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain qualifications — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly — and applicants in those categories are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service) before applying. No specific subject prerequisites, no separate minimum GPA gate beyond the 21/33 ranking threshold, and no prior ECTS/SSD requirement (this is a bachelor programme, so the SSD-credit logic that applies to unibz master admissions is not relevant here). Language requirements are a hard admission gate — failing them means exclusion from the procedure before any ranking. Under national rules, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of two programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same degree class (explicitly: not L-18 with another L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of course content — which matters here because the sibling Bachelor in Economics and Management is also L-18 and therefore cannot be combined with this one. Credit points from previous university studies can be recognised only after enrolment, and only where the exams taken at the previous university are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language requirement is a hard exclusion gate — failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure entirely, not merely a lower score. Requirements are defined by POSITION (1st/2nd/3rd language), not by which specific language: your first language is the one you are strongest in (B2 or C1), your third is the one you are weakest in or an absolute beginner in. Entry: B2 in the 1st language, B2 in the 2nd language, no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2, per the Common European Framework of Reference. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and only recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. B1 in the third language is the minimum to sit curricular exams in that language, and if the first semester is taught only in English while English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January to take all first-semester exams. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2; three-week intensive courses run in September (2026/27: 01–18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 h/day) and A1 beginner courses are now offered ONLY in that September window and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there. Extensive courses (4 h/week) run during semesters, intensive courses (6 h/day) between semesters; all Language Centre courses are free of charge. Higher-than-required levels earn up to 3 ranking bonus points. For this programme the language gate is the single most consequential requirement: it accounted for 29 EU exclusions in Early Bird, 10 in Late, and both of the only two non-EU applicants.
application_deadline_eu: THREE sessions were open for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment in 2026/27 — this programme, unlike the Bachelor in Economics and Management, did receive an Additional Application Session. (1) EARLY BIRD — application 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08, by noon local time (28/05 - 08/07/2026). (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, by noon local time (18/08 - 04/09/2026). AS OF THE VERIFICATION DATE 2026-08-29 THE ADDITIONAL SESSION IS STILL OPEN, with the deadline six days away; the unibz additional-application-session page lists this programme as 'Application possible'. Applicants excluded in an earlier session may re-apply in a later one, and EU applicants may apply to more than one study programme — the 2026/27 ranking lists show at least ten Applicant IDs that were excluded on language grounds in Early Bird and then admitted in the Late session after fixing their certification.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (Early Bird, unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have no Late Application and no Additional Session — 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies. Downstream 2026/27 dates matched Early Bird: ranking by 2026-05-27, first instalment by 2026-06-05 (noon), enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 (noon). Universitaly pre-enrolment is mandatory after paying the first instalment, and admission on the ranking list is granted 'with reservation' until the Italian consulate confirms directly to unibz. HARD REALITY CHECK for 2026/27: this single window produced only two non-EU applicants and both were excluded for failing the language requirements, so no non-EU student was admitted to this programme at all. For a non-EU applicant targeting 2027/28, the window will fall around early March to late April 2027 and the binding preparation task is certifying B2 in a second language (German or Italian) well before it opens.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION (uploaded in the unibz Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) a valid ID card or passport, front and back — an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document means exclusion from the admission procedure; (2) the completed online application form, including the self-declaration of grades for the four subject areas plus two extra subjects for each of the two relevant high-school years (secondary schools in Germany: insert the 'Jahreszeugnis' grades, or if unavailable the average of the two 'Halbjahreszeugnisse' with decimal place); (3) a copy of the relevant school report cards for any self-declared year completed abroad; (4) official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; (5) optionally, language certificates for the entry-level proof and the bonus-point calculation; (6) the diploma of the qualification if already obtained, otherwise at enrolment. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Once sent, the application cannot be modified, and forms that are filled in but not correctly submitted are disregarded — one Late-session applicant was excluded in 2026/27 precisely for not providing the required documents. AT ENROLMENT, for a foreign secondary-school qualification: the secondary school diploma; an official translation of the diploma into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. NOTE: the structured 'study career' Excel template that unibz requires for master's applications is NOT part of this bachelor procedure. Transfer students from another Italian university must additionally submit a copy of the transfer application filed at their previous university to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. unibz may request further documents in case of doubt and can exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the admission qualification is not valid.
entry_exam_or_test: NO admission entrance exam of any kind — unibz does not use its own subject test, TOLC-I, TOLC-E, CENT-S, SAT or GMAT/GRE for this programme. Admission is purely dossier/ranking based.

Language proficiency exams (optional route, only if you cannot prove your levels by diploma or recognised certificate): organised online by the unibz Language Centre. 2026/27 Early Bird sittings 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 + 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late Application sittings 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Registration is done inside the application portal under 'enrol for language exams', and only after an application has been created under 'create/manage applications'. Note: only B2-level exams can be booked, and no Language Centre exam sittings are listed for the Additional Application Session.

Compulsory mathematics test — AFTER admission, not for admission. The faculty runs a preparatory course in mathematics in English before the first semester (2026/27: 21–25/09/2026) and every new student must sit a compulsory test at the end of it. A negative result or non-participation triggers OFA (see ofa_rules).

Third-language placement test — after admission, for students who cannot certify their third language; the result determines the assigned language-learning path aimed at reaching B2 as soon as possible.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/economics-management/fees — EUR 1,200 per year for students within the normal programme length, split into two instalments of EUR 600. The 1st instalment includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and, during the admission procedure, is the payment that secures the admitted place (2026/27 admission deadlines: 05/06/2026 Early Bird, 06/08/2026 Late, 25/09/2026 Additional). Once enrolled, the faculty fee calendar is 1st instalment by 13/10/2026 and 2nd instalment by 31/03/2027 (the admission PDF states more generally 'by March of the following year'). Students beyond the normal programme length (fuori corso) pay EUR 1,500 (EUR 900 + EUR 600). Late payment of the second instalment incurs a EUR 30 fine and blocks the online account, exam registration and transfers to other universities or programmes. No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Full exemption (paying only the EUR 16 stamp) applies to students with a disability recognised under art. 3 para. 1 of Law 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more — the health-authority certificate must be handed in at the start of the academic year — and to foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Freemover students studying abroad for both semesters pay nothing; for the first semester only, the 2nd instalment is still due by 31/03. Students concluding their studies by 31 October owe no annual fee; by 31 March, only the EUR 16 stamp duty. Holders of a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees, usually in March–April, though the refund does not cover late-payment fines.
official_call_url: No separate call/manifesto document is published in English for this programme — the admission-information PDF functions as the official call. The underlying legal act is Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025 ('delibera del Consiglio di Facoltà della Facoltà di Economia n. 142 dd. 15.09.2025'), which approved the 2026/27 selection criteria; it is cited in both ranking-list PDFs but is not published as a standalone downloadable file on unibz.it. Related official pages: application portal https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ , additional-application-session page https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/additional-application-session , study plan https://www.unibz.it/en/faculties/economics-management/bachelor-tourism-sport-event-management/study-plan/ [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes: 1) CYCLE STATUS — all data is the 2026/27 cycle. Unlike most unibz programmes, this one is NOT fully closed as of the verification date (2026-08-29): the Early Bird and Late sessions are finished with signed ranking lists, but the Additional Application Session (18/08–04/09/2026, EU citizens only) is still open with about six days remaining, and its ranking list is due by 18/09/2026. The 2027/28 call, quotas and dates are not yet published. 2) Both official PDFs carry 'Latest update: 24.08.2026' and are explicitly marked 'Subject to change'. 3) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING — unibz publishes no percentage split of teaching hours per language. The distribution given in teaching_language was reconstructed from the public course-offering page and individual syllabi; the syllabus evidence cited (Marketing = English, Managerial Economics for TSE = Italian) is from the 2024/2025 academic year, and course-level teaching languages can be reassigned between years. The trilingual classification itself is certain; only the weighting is uncertain. 4) QUOTA ARITHMETIC — the two completed sessions admitted 118 EU candidates against a published EU quota of 100 (80 + 20). This is read directly from the signed ranking lists and is not a transcription error, but unibz publishes no explanation for exceeding the quota; the plausible mechanisms (rollover of places from admitted candidates who did not pay, plus faculty discretion in an undersubscribed programme) are inferred, not documented. 5) ADDITIONAL SESSION PLACES — the additional-application-session page confirms 'Application possible' for this programme but does not publish a number of available places. 6) FIRST INTAKE YEAR is not published; the 'not a new programme' assessment rests on 2024/2025 syllabi and a 2025/26 edition of the official PDFs. 7) OFFICIAL CALL — there is no standalone English call/manifesto PDF; Faculty Council Resolution 142 of 15.09.2025 is cited in the ranking lists but is not downloadable, so official_call_url is a best-effort answer. 8) SCHOLARSHIPS — the live unibz Study Grants page confirms the categories and the non-EU residence restriction but does not restate the EUR 1,680–6,960 range or the 27/30 merit threshold, so those two figures are carried from prior unibz materials and may be out of date. 9) NON-EU VISA FIGURES — the EUR 800/month subsistence, EUR 36,000 bachelor total and 20 h/week work cap are general unibz/Italian rules and do not appear in this programme's own admission PDF. 10) TURKEY'S CREDENTIAL TIER (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification) is inferred from Turkey's Lisbon Convention membership, since unibz publishes the rule by tier rather than by country. 11) The ranking-list PDFs are published only in Italian and German; the English admission PDF does not report cut-off scores, so every cut-off figure here was read from the bilingual IT/DE documents. 12) CAMPUS — the Bruneck-to-Bolzano relocation from year two is stated in the official 2026/27 brochure and is therefore certain; the accompanying report that the Bruneck master's programme is suspended for 2026/27 comes from secondary reporting rather than a unibz page and is contextual only. 13) The 'effectively-closed' verdict for English-only candidates is an interpretation, but it rests on two hard facts rather than one: the B2/B2 position rule combined with 41 documented language exclusions across the two 2026/27 sessions (29 + 10 EU and 2 non-EU), and compulsory first-year courses that are actually delivered in German and Italian.
